models._description: Certificate key — Fernet symmetric-key decryption helper for EDI payloads
Company — owns the EDI proxy users

behavioral_notes.observation: The account_edi_proxy_client.user record is the per-company identity on a proxy/access-point service: it stores id_client (unique server-issued client id), edi_identification (the address the user is reachable at on the network, e.g. the VAT for Peppol), private_key_id (a certificate.key RSA private key, domain public=False), refresh_token (readable only by base.group_system), proxy_type (extensible Selection — e.g. peppol, l10n_it_edi, nemhandel) and edi_mode (prod/test/demo). _register_proxy_user() first generates an RSA keypair via certificate.key._generate_rsa_private_key, then POSTs {dbuuid, company_id, edi_identification, public_key(PEM), proxy_type} to '<server_url>/iap/account_edi/2/create_user' and persists the returned id_client + refresh_token as a new user. A UNIQUE index '(company_id, proxy_type, edi_mode) WHERE active' enforces one active enrolment per (company, network, mode); demo mode short-circuits to fake credentials with no network call. This enrolment/identity handshake is invisible in metadata.

_make_request(url, params, auth_type) wraps every proxy call: it builds a JSON-RPC 2.0 envelope {jsonrpc:'2.0', method:'call', params, id:uuid4}, hard-blocks any call while edi_mode=='demo' (raises AccountEdiProxyError 'block_demo_mode'), then requests.post()s with a 30s timeout (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT) and the OdooEdiProxyAuth signer attached as auth=. Network/HTTP/JSON errors (ConnectionError, MissingSchema, Timeout, HTTPError, ValueError) are collapsed into AccountEdiProxyError('connection_error'). It then inspects response['result']['proxy_error']: on 'refresh_token_expired' it calls _renew_token(), commits the cursor so the new token is not lost, and retries with hmac auth; on 'no_such_user' it deactivates the local user (active=False); on 'invalid_signature' it raises a database-duplication warning pointing at Odoo Access Point. This retry/renew/deactivate logic and the cursor commit are runtime semantics absent from metadata.

Every authenticated request is signed by OdooEdiProxyAuth (a requests.auth.AuthBase). It crafts a canonical message 'timestamp|url-path|id_client|sorted-query-params|sorted-json-body', adds headers odoo-edi-client-id and odoo-edi-timestamp, then signs one of two ways: (hmac, default) HMAC-SHA256 over the message keyed by the base64-decoded refresh_token; or (asymmetric) an RSA signature via private_key._sign(message, formatting='base64') — used as a fallback to resync the token when databases desynchronise (restore-from-backup / un-neutralised copy). Signature + type go into odoo-edi-signature / odoo-edi-signature-type headers. This preserves message integrity, lets the server check access rights/account validity, and stops two databases sharing credentials (the 24h-expiring refresh_token). Cryptographic signing is invisible to ORM metadata.

_renew_token() locks the user row (lock_for_update; silently returns on LockError to avoid contention), POSTs to '/iap/account_edi/1/renew_token' and stores the new refresh_token (sudo); refresh tokens expire after 24h precisely so two databases cannot keep querying with the same credentials. Inbound documents are encrypted by the proxy with the user's public key: _decrypt_data() RSA-decrypts the symmetric key via private_key_id._decrypt, then Fernet-decrypts the payload via certificate.key._account_edi_fernet_decrypt — i.e. envelope encryption (RSA-wrapped Fernet symmetric key). proxy_type's Selection is empty and _get_proxy_urls returns {} / _get_proxy_identification returns False (TO OVERRIDE), so concrete networks (Peppol, l10n_it_edi, nemhandel) are wired up by sibling localization modules, not here.

No frontend assets: 0 JS files, 0 XML templates, 0 OWL components, 0 registry registrations, 0 patches, no asset bundles. The only UI is a server-rendered form/list on account_edi_proxy_client.user; all behaviour is backend Python plumbing.

1 outbound HTTP call site using the requests SDK (no vendored SDK, no stored api-key field). The single egress path is account_edi_proxy_client.user._make_request -> requests.post to '<server_url>/iap/account_edi/2/create_user', '/iap/account_edi/1/renew_token' and other proxy endpoints resolved from _get_proxy_urls() (the Odoo IAP / access-point host per proxy_type+edi_mode). Requests are signed with OdooEdiProxyAuth (HMAC-SHA256 over refresh_token, or RSA asymmetric fallback). No endpoints are hard-coded in this base module — URLs come from the extending localization. This is the access-point connectivity layer for e-invoicing networks (Peppol, etc.).

it_architecture.application: account_edi_proxy_client (EDI proxy / access-point client — application component extending account, talks to Odoo's IAP e-invoicing access-point service)
information_flows: egress: account_edi_proxy_client.user._register_proxy_user -> POST <server_url>/iap/account_edi/2/create_user with {dbuuid, company_id, edi_identification, public_key(PEM), proxy_type} -> stores id_client + refresh_token
egress: account_edi_proxy_client.user._make_request -> signed JSON-RPC 2.0 POST to the proxy host (OdooEdiProxyAuth signs message timestamp|path|id_client|query|body)
ingress: proxy returns RSA-wrapped Fernet-encrypted documents -> _decrypt_data RSA-decrypts symmetric key then Fernet-decrypts payload
control: proxy_error 'refresh_token_expired' -> _renew_token + commit + retry; 'no_such_user' -> deactivate user; 'invalid_signature' -> database-duplication error
extension point: _get_proxy_urls / _get_proxy_identification / proxy_type Selection extended by localization modules (Peppol, l10n_it_edi, nemhandel) to bind concrete networks

capabilities: Enrol Company as an E-Invoicing Network Identity (register proxy user)
Authenticate & Sign Requests to the EDI Access Point (HMAC / RSA)
Maintain Network Credentials (id_client, refresh token, RSA keypair)
Exchange E-Invoice Documents over an Access-Point Proxy (Peppol / IAP)
Provide a Pluggable Transport for Country/Network Localizations
value_streams: Network Onboarding: generate RSA keypair -> POST create_user with public key + edi_identification -> persist id_client + refresh_token -> active proxy user
Document Exchange: build signed JSON-RPC request -> POST to proxy host -> on token expiry renew + retry -> receive & decrypt response payload
information_concepts: certificate.key (RSA private key used to sign and to unwrap encrypted payloads)
policies: UNIQUE(id_client): a server-issued client id maps to exactly one user
UNIQUE(company_id, proxy_type, edi_mode) WHERE active: one active enrolment per company per network per mode
refresh_token readable only by base.group_system; record managed only by base.group_system, read-only for account.group_account_invoice
demo edi_mode is hard-blocked from any real proxy call (block_demo_mode)
refresh_token expires after 24h to prevent two databases sharing credentials; row-locked renew with cursor commit
all authenticated requests must carry an HMAC-SHA256 (or RSA asymmetric fallback) signature over a canonical message
stakeholders: Accountant / Billing user (consumes e-invoicing via localization built on this transport)
Company / Tax-registered entity (the enrolled network identity)
Odoo IAP / Access-Point service (the proxy host)
Localization developer (extends proxy_type and proxy URLs)
metrics: active proxy users per company / proxy_type / edi_mode
connection_error / invalid_signature occurrence rate (proxy call health)

classification.rationale: account_edi_proxy_client is e-invoicing transport and identity infrastructure: it depends only on account + certificate and adds no accounting value of its own. It provides the signed, encrypted client that lets a company enrol on and exchange documents with an external EDI access point (Odoo's IAP service / networks like Peppol) — the network-and-identity plumbing beneath the structured invoices that primary activities (sale -> customer invoice) already produced. In Stabell & Fjeldstad terms the access point it connects to is itself a value network (mediating membership/identity and document interchange between parties over shared infrastructure), but at the enterprise activity level this module is a support function, not a primary one: it carries and authenticates accounting documents rather than creating them. It maps to APQC 9.0 Manage Financial Resources, specifically the AR/AP compliance facet (9.2.x Process accounts receivable / 9.5.x Process accounts payable) where the structured electronic delivery and legal acknowledgement of the account.move invoice occurs. proxy_type and the proxy URLs are deliberate extension stubs, confirming this is reusable transport plumbing subclassed by localizations, not a revenue- or production-bearing process.

standard_capabilities: per-company proxy-user enrolment with server-issued id_client and an RSA keypair
signed JSON-RPC 2.0 transport to an EDI access point (HMAC-SHA256 over canonical message, RSA asymmetric fallback)
automatic 24h refresh-token renewal with retry, plus database-duplication / desync detection
envelope decryption of inbound documents (RSA-wrapped Fernet symmetric key)
prod / test / demo operating modes with demo hard-blocking real calls
pluggable proxy_type + proxy-URL hooks for localization networks (Peppol, l10n_it_edi, nemhandel)
credential security: refresh_token gated to base.group_system, manager-only write
typical_fits: country/network e-invoicing modules (Peppol, Italian SdI, Danish Nemhandel) that extend proxy_type and _get_proxy_urls to bind a concrete access point
exchanging UBL/CII e-invoices over Peppol via the Odoo access point without managing certificates manually
running in test/demo mode for onboarding before going to prod
common_gaps: no concrete network ships here — base proxy_type Selection is empty and _get_proxy_urls returns {}; a localization is required to do anything
endpoints are not hard-coded — the IAP/proxy host is supplied by the extending module
no inbound dispatch/routing of decrypted documents to account.move (that lives in the consuming localization)
no dedicated frontend/dashboard — only an admin form/list on the proxy user
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['account_edi_proxy_client.user']._fields['proxy_type'].selection  # which networks are installed (empty in base)
odoo shell: u = env['account_edi_proxy_client.user'].search([], limit=1); u and u._get_server_url()  # resolved proxy host (KeyError without a localization)
curl: signing is via OdooEdiProxyAuth headers odoo-edi-client-id / odoo-edi-timestamp / odoo-edi-signature — see models/account_edi_proxy_auth.py to reproduce the canonical message
